description: Render a polar sky chart of a satellite's pass over a location: where to look, with the moon, planets and stars in place. Returns the charted pass (the same row find_passes gives) and a one-line summary as JSON, then the image, a PNG of 800 by 897 pixels, about 120 KB. By default it charts the next pass; give time (a pass's rise or peak from find_passes or find_best_pass) to chart that pass, with the same minElevation it came from. A geostationary satellite has no passes: stationary says where to point instead, with no image. A time more than 30 days from the orbital elements' epoch is refused. Read-only, free, no key needed; up to 120 requests per 60 seconds per IP address. A bad input or a failure comes back as an error result (isError) whose text names the problem and what to change. A place name is looked up with OpenStreetMap (one lookup a second, cached), which can add a few seconds; lat and lon or a grid square need none. A heavy call: one at a time per caller; another waits up to 20 seconds, then is refused as busy.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

minElevation.description: lowest elevation that counts: a pass must climb above it, and rise and set are when it crosses it, in degrees above the horizon (0 to 90). Default 10.

mode.description: "visual" (default): naked-eye passes, sunlit while the sky is dark; "radio": every line-of-sight pass, day or night.

satellite.description: NORAD catalog number (as a number or a string) or a name, e.g. 25544, "25544" or "iss".

skyType.description: how dark the observer's sky is, for the visual rating as on seeksat.com: "city" (stars to magnitude 3.5), "suburban" (stars to magnitude 4.5), "rural" (stars to magnitude 5.5), "dark" (stars to magnitude 6.5). Default "suburban".

time.description: charts the pass around this time (a pass's rise or peak from find_passes or find_best_pass). Default: the next pass from now. ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00:00-06:00"; a time with no offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00", is read in the observer's time zone, and the result echoes how it was read (interpretedAs). A local time the clocks skip at a daylight-saving change is moved forward, with a note.

windowHours.description: how far ahead to look, in hours, up to 240 (10 days). Default 72. Only used to find the next pass when no time is given.
